intro: A paddle, a ball and a wall of bricks. Knock the ball into the wall to break it. Play together, up to four paddles on one wall, or race each other on a wall each.
inspiredBy: Paddle-and-bricks games go back to the arcades of the mid 1970s. Bricks is our own take: our own walls, power-ups, colours and sounds.
goal: Co-op: clear wall after wall as a team, for the best score you can, before your balls run out. Versus: be the first to clear your wall (or the last one with a ball) to take the round; win the set number of rounds to take the match.
howToPlay: Join with your phone. In the lobby choose Co-op or Versus, add computer partners or rivals if you like, then press {bolt} to start.
Move your paddle with the stick. Push it past its ring to go faster.
The ball starts on your paddle: press {bolt} to launch it. The dotted line shows which way it will go.
Where the ball lands on your paddle decides where it goes: the middle sends it straight up, the ends send it out wide. Moving as it lands drags it the way you're moving.
The ball gets faster the longer it stays in play.
Tough bricks take two or three hits (one pip per hit left). Grey steel never breaks. Red charges blow up the bricks around them, and set off other charges.

Broken bricks sometimes drop a power-up: catch it with your paddle. W makes it wider, 3 splits every ball into three, L gives you a laser (hold {bolt} to fire), S slows the ball, C catches the ball (press {bolt} to let go), and + is a spare ball.
In co-op the paddles share the bottom edge and can't pass each other, and the team shares the balls. Lose the last ball in play and a spare comes in; out of spares, and the game is over.
In versus everyone has the same wall. Catch J and press {drop} to drop a row of junk bricks on your rivals' walls; catch − and press {drop} to shrink their paddles.
Press ❚❚ on your phone to pause.
steering: Move the paddle with the stick
tips: Break a channel up the side and get the ball above the wall: it does the work for you up there.
Every five bricks one ball breaks without touching a paddle adds one to the multiplier.
Save the ends of the paddle for when you need an angle: a ball off the middle is the safest return.
With the catch, hold the ball, slide to where you want it and let go.
Charges next to each other go off in a chain: aim for them.
